rationale:
Decision: resubmit the verified best design, the raced iteration 7 candidate with kd 0.35 and line_loss 'last_direction'. This is a revert from the kd 0.4 test and from the search_left version described in the authorized entity1 text.

Evidence: the outcome table records the raced iteration 7 design as kd 0.35, ki 0.5, kp 2.0, base_speed 1.5, line_loss 'last_direction', scoring 344.50 with 17 of 20 oval finishes (mean oval score 850). Its s-bend (137.7) and slalom (45.8) runs still end off track, with 1.15 and 1.25 line-loss events per run. The entity1 text describes the same design as kd 0.25 to 0.4 with line_loss 'search_left', but the outcome table does not match that description, and the 344.5 score belongs to the kd 0.35 / last_direction record. I have not tested search_left.

Why not kd 0.4: its baseline is misstated. Testing kd 0.4 against the 'kd 0.25' baseline would confound the result with the already-raced kd 0.35 change. The critique is also right that kd amplifies noise and makes the line-loss onset step larger, and its falsification rule has gaps (the 0.222 to 0.25 band and the slalom target have no decision rule). Those concerns are accepted as reasons not to advance kd 0.4 now.

Why not search_left: the record that produced the gain is last_direction, so switching direction now would reverse the only verified improvement without a clean test.

What I kept: every value of the verified 344.5 design. What I changed: nothing. The change from the earlier draft is that I no longer rely on the unverified search_left description.

Expected result: about 344 on the development set, with oval finishes near 17 of 20 and s-bend and slalom still failing. Next iteration, if a single-variable test is run, it should start from this record and state its baseline explicitly.
